items.summary: US stocks rallied on Nov 9, with the S&P 500 rebounding from its biggest weekly drop since April 2025. A slide in oil prices tempered inflation concerns while tech shares rose even as Nvidia fell 4.2% amid controversy over CEO Jensen Huang following an internal investigation into whether a foreign intelligence effort targeted him. Analysts at Morgan Stanley and UBS called last week's AI selloff an overreaction, though the S&P posted its biggest daily gain since April 8.
items.title: US Stocks Jump as Oil Slide Eases Inflation Fears; Nvidia Slumps

items.summary: Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating an affair between Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. He spoke with Huang on Monday after reports that US intelligence believed he was targeted in a Beijing espionage campaign. China called the allegations groundless; Nvidia launched its own probe and found no compromise of secrets or national security. Trump said Huang had 'no idea' she was a spy and described him as an honorable guy who will be in good shape. He added Xi Jinping would raise it at their next meeting, which he is sure about.
items.title: Trump Says FBI Investigating Nvidia Chief's Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy

items.summary: Wired reported that Nvidia's Jensen Huang hired crisis communications firm Heller Inc., known for handling sex scandals, at least a year before publicly acknowledging an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. The report followed a New York Times story about Megaspeed acquiring nearly $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips and its CEO Alice Huang appearing beside him in Taipei. Nvidia acknowledged the affair without naming her and announced an independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Hired Crisis PR Firm Before Acknowledging Affair

items.summary: Culper Research, a New York-based short seller firm, flagged an unusually close relationship between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed six months before the spy scandal emerged. U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by China to influence chip export controls. Culper's May 13 report called their ties 'uncomfortably close.' The allegations remain unverified.
items.title: Short Seller Flagged Nvidia CEO Ties Before Spy Scandal Emerged

items.summary: The affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed—a major customer of Nvidia chips—has escalated into a national security concern. U.S. intelligence surveillance reportedly showed she was funneling information to the Chinese government. The revelation contradicts earlier statements from spokesperson John Rizzo, who described their interactions as routine business dealings.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces White House Scrutiny Over Alleged Spy Ties

items.summary: Herald van der Linde, HSBC's head of equity strategy for Asia-Pacific, told The Straits Times that Singapore must attract more innovative companies to grow its stock market. He noted regulators have revitalised the exchange and schemes like the $6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme have placed $5.4 billion across 14 asset managers as at September. Singapore recorded five IPOs raising US$868 million in the first half of 2026, versus Malaysia's 36 raising about US$1.34 billion and Hong Kong's 13 specialist technology listings alone. Van der Linde said a steady pipeline of companies is needed and pointed to government efforts through a growth capital work group convened earlier in 2026 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry.
items.title: HSBC Chief Urges Singapore To Attract More Tech Listings

items.summary: Samsung's Galaxy SmartTag 3 is now available in the US, promising a smaller and lighter design than earlier models, up to 550 days of battery life, iOS compatibility, an NFC-powered Lost Mode, Left Behind Alerts, and an IP67 rating. The article's main concern is that Bluetooth Channel Sounding, which powers Compass View for fine distance finding, works only with Galaxy phones running Bluetooth 6.0 — the Z Fold 8 Ultra, Z Fold 8, S26 Ultra, and S26 Plus — not iPhones or older models. Samsung cites a press release stating nearly 900 million Galaxy devices exist on its Find Network. Apple announced Channel Sounding support at WWDC for future Bluetooth 6.3 hardware expected in years, while Google's open Find Hub already supports multiple manufacturers.
items.title: Samsung SmartTag 3's Bluetooth ranging locked to Galaxy phones

items.summary: Reports indicate Samsung may introduce a paid subscription for its Galaxy AI Premium features, potentially starting at $4.99 per month or $47.99 annually. Subscribers could receive usage limits four times higher than the free plan plus access to exclusive tools like AI-generated videos and Bixby Action. Basic functions such as Photo Assist would remain available without unlimited use. Samsung has not confirmed a release date.
items.title: Samsung Considers Paid Galaxy AI Subscription Tiers

items.summary: The Ministry of Health responds to a letter from Ho See Ling about parents facing strained relations with adult children, assuring them that distressing family conflicts need not be faced alone. National Mental Health Office director Harold Tan directs those in emotional difficulty to call or text the 24/7 national MindLine service at 1771 for listening support and referrals, while community mental health teams, primary care providers such as GP clinics and polyclinics also offer continued help; he encourages parents and caregivers to seek assistance early. Further details are available on the Ministry of Health website.
items.title: MOH Director Points Parents to Mental Health Support

items.summary: Alice Marwick, writing on Nov 9, 2026, frames the recent Democratic electoral gains as a mandate for technology regulation beyond artificial intelligence. She notes that winning candidates campaigned against Big Tech and that ballot initiatives to curb data centers passed around the country. Marwick asked scholars and policy experts what they would add to their wishlists at state or federal levels. Responses span affordability—citing New York City’s Click to Cancel law; privacy, including revising the 1974 Privacy Act; advertising transparency over bot activity on social platforms; cracking down on AI-driven scams by banning crypto ATMs and holding Meta liable for scam ads; enabling researcher data access like Europe’s Digital Services Act; expanding regulatory capacity after Trump-era cuts; and reviving the Office of Technology Assessment at an estimated $30 million, possibly funded by a tech tax. Marwick stresses these measures may not be flashy but could benefit average Americans.
items.title: Scholars Outline Tech Regulation Priorities Beyond AI

items.summary: France attributed a supermarket freezer attack, in which fridges overheated and caught fire forcing staff to discard spoiled meat and melted ice-cream, to hackers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. France’s foreign minister called it an act of “unprecedented scale and unprecedented aggression” promising Europe-wide sanctions. Sophos’ Rafe Pilling said default passwords were used and that the French incident likely connects to a recent wave of rogue defrosting hacks across Europe; however, those attacks remain unattributed while this announcement is the first to implicate Iran’s state in such hacks.
items.title: France Blames Iran for Supermarket Freezer Hack Amid Regional Cyber Escalation

items.summary: Foxglove, a tech equity campaign group, obtained WhatsApp messages under the Freedom of Information Act showing Palantir urging former health minister Zubir Ahmed to extend its AI technology into GP records. The lobbying came in February despite GP data being expressly ruled out of scope from Palantir’s existing £330m contract with NHS England. Donald Campbell of Foxglove called it “lobbying to hoover up yet more” sensitive personal data, while Dr Tom Dolphin of the British Medical Association warned it could undermine patient trust. Palantir said its exchanges reflected that data sharing can improve care and that rollout decisions rest with the government. The review continues as ministers weigh extending versus replacing the contract by 2029.
items.title: Palantir Lobbied Health Minister Over NHS GP Data

items.summary: Japanese gaming company SEGA disclosed that a breach at its third-party newsletter provider ARARA exposed the email addresses of 2.2 million subscribers, plus 92,300 records with additional information yet to be determined across 11 newsletters linked to SEGA and SEGA Fave products. The investigation found no customer names or passwords were compromised, and no confirmed evidence of misuse exists as SEGA works with ARARA on the case.
items.title: SEGA Discloses Newsletter Data Breach Exposing Millions of Email Addresses

items.summary: Scott Wiener, a California state senator who won Nancy Pelosi's open San Francisco congressional seat in a tight race on Friday, says he is ready to help shape federal AI policy. He recently spoke with MIT Technology Review hours after his victory and cited an METR report interpreted as evidence of Anthropic achieving recursive self-improvement, saying it shows Congress risks running out of time to act before year's end. Wiener authored SB 1047 in 2024, which was vetoed by Governor Gavin Newsom; he also sponsored the signed SB 53. His campaign received over $3 million from Public First Action, an AI-regulation nonprofit funded by Anthropic, drawing criticism that he is too close to Big Tech—claims Wiener rejects. He expressed interest in serving on a congressional select committee and emphasized whistleblower protections, testing requirements, auditing, a kill switch, and opposing broad federal preemption of state laws.
items.title: Scott Wiener Vows Federal AI Regulation After Winning San Francisco Seat

items.summary: Security researcher Sean Bales disclosed more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities in the N-central remote management platform, publishing proof-of-concept exploits in a GitHub repository called Able2Shell. The disclosures include authentication bypasses and remote code execution flaws that could allow attackers to take over systems as the nable user. In response, N-able took its hosted environments offline across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific on November 9 and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers until a hotfix is ready.
items.title: N-able Shuts Down N-central After Researcher Discloses Zero-Days

items.summary: In an Edmunds EV Range Test, the new 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ drove 539 miles on a single charge with its 122 kWh battery and 800V architecture. It beat its EPA estimate of up to 467 miles by 72 miles, becoming Edmunds' longest-range electric sedan tested, ahead of the Lucid Air but behind the Cadillac Escalade IQ at 558 miles. The test used a mix of city and highway driving at an average speed of 40 mph with climate control set to auto at 72 degrees.
items.title: Mercedes EQS Sets Range Record in Edmunds Test

items.summary: Democratic Sens. Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse pitched their bipartisan permitting reform bill, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), as a way to make lives more affordable while holding data centers accountable for costs, ahead of an evening Senate vote on whether it advances to the floor. The bill needs 60 votes to proceed. Heinrich cited Brattle Group estimates that BAAJA would force data centers to pay $35 billion more over a decade; the Rhodium Group forecasted household electricity bills could fall by $50 to $78 in 2040, with pollution dropping between 1% and 18%. Environmental groups like NRDC oppose it despite changes. Utilities signed on after revisions, though House passage remains uncertain during the lame duck period.
items.title: Senate Permitting Bill Faces Crucial Vote Amid Bipartisan Pushback

items.summary: Researchers at KAIST and the Georgia Institute of Technology developed a bare porous polyacrylonitrile membrane that separates crude oil molecules without high-temperature heating. When crude oil passes through it, heavy hydrocarbons stick to pore walls, narrowing them below 2 nanometers. The team reported permeation rates approximately 23 times higher than previous membranes while holding performance stable for 28 consecutive days. Process simulations suggested using the membrane as a pretreatment step could reduce energy consumption by 31.6%, carbon dioxide emissions by 37.6%, cooling water usage by 20.7%, and operating costs by 36%. The researchers said refineries could adopt it with simple retrofits, though they noted it cannot replace distillation proper. Professor Ryan Lively of Georgia Tech called for industry to consider the technology.
items.title: KAIST and Georgia Tech Membrane Cuts Oil Refining Energy Use

items.summary: An Oilprice.com article by James Durso argues that the Sudanese civil war should be treated by Washington as a national security issue rather than only a humanitarian emergency. It outlines strategic stakes including Red Sea shipping, Iran’s growing ties with Khartoum after diplomatic restoration in 2024, counterterrorism risks from ungoverned territory, and Sudan’s mineral resources such as gold, uranium, and chromium. Durso calls for civilian-led political transition, sustained diplomacy, and accountability measures rather than military solutions or indefinite stalemate. The piece notes a June 2026 joint statement reaffirming sovereignty and an inclusive process, without attributing independent verification to any claim.
items.title: Oilprice Author Frames Sudan War as U.S. Strategic Concern

items.summary: On November 9, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced its approval of two applications filed by Mutual Federal Bancorp, MHC and MFB Bancorp, Inc., both based in Chicago, Illinois. The approvals permit the organization to establish a new top-tier holding company, MFB Bancorp, Inc., which would become a savings and loan holding company through acquisition of Mutual Federal Bank, also located in Chicago, Illinois. Media inquiries are directed to (202) 452-2955 or email at press@federalreserve.gov. The announcement was released for distribution at 4:00 p.m. EST on Monday.
items.title: Federal Reserve Approves Mutual Federal Bancorp Restructuring Applications

items.summary: Nvidia's share price fell after the company said it was investigating CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. The report frames the drop as tied to the investigation into the alleged affair, without confirming any wrongdoing or providing further detail on the claims.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall After Investigation Into Jensen Huang

items.summary: A proposed class action filed Monday (Nov. 9) in San Jose federal court accuses Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US authorities say is a Chinese intelligence asset. The complaint claims the undisclosed affair raised national security concerns threatening Nvidia's reputation and business prospects. Shares fell 4.3 per cent to roughly $190 billion in market value. Nvidia announced an internal probe on Sunday but did not comment publicly; shareholders led by Mark Kistenmacher seek unspecified damages.
items.title: Nvidia and Jensen Huang Face Shareholder Lawsuit Over Alleged Concealment of Spy Ties

items.summary: Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, is being investigated by his own company over an alleged extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a former CEO described as possibly a Chinese spy. The report frames the matter within US-China rivalry in artificial intelligence and national security concerns about chip access. Megaspeed denies any illegitimate use of its purchases; China denies espionage. Nvidia states there is no evidence that anything was passed on and has launched an internal inquiry. Huang says he will co-operate, retains board backing and Trump's support, but faces questions over whether secrets were shared with Beijing or others while awaiting the investigation's conclusion.
items.title: Nvidia Investigates Jensen Huang Over Alleged Spy Affair

items.summary: A Bloomberg Opinion commentary argues Jensen Huang is more central than Nvidia itself, warning his affair with an alleged Chinese spy could damage the chipmaker and wider AI markets. The piece notes Nvidia’s US$4.5 trillion market cap and its lending of credit to customers through roughly US$300 billion in support over three years. It raises concerns that dealmakers may step back from vendor financing, slowing data centre growth as bond spreads widen and a bear market looms.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Scandal Threatens AI Sector Confidence

items.summary: Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang face mounting pressure from lawmakers after he admitted an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. Members of Congress in both parties are pushing stronger export controls to limit chip sales to Beijing, alongside investigations into the company's dealings. Sen. Richard Blumenthal said Nvidia says it will investigate but emphasized the need for a Senate investigation. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries supports stricter provisions and wants a full briefing on the issue. The Commerce Department and White House did not respond to requests for comment.
items.title: Congress pushes Nvidia export controls amid spy scandal

items.summary: Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, according to Politico. The disclosure is galvanizing lawmakers who want stricter export controls on Nvidia chips and deeper scrutiny of the company, even as Trump has defended Huang and lobbied against some restrictions.
items.title: Nvidia's Spy Scandal Fuels US Efforts to Restrict Its China Exports

items.summary: Jonathan Liew argues that tech leaders who backed Donald Trump have been humbled by recent electoral losses. He points to the US midterms, where 46 of 47 ballot measures on datacentres were defeated and voters punished big-tech-enabling politicians in Texas and Ohio despite heavy outspending. Markets then fell sharply as investors reacted to what he calls the biggest progressive landslide in 52 years. Liew questions whether such popular repudiation should trigger more democratic accountability from industry, media and politics, while noting that UK AI policy advances quietly under a Labour government with little public opposition. He ends by citing Goldman Sachs's note expecting datacentre moratoria to fade, leaving the tech class's next move uncertain.
items.title: Tech billionaires' Trump gamble backfires amid datacentre defeat

items.summary: Jensen Huang has admitted having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy reportedly central to the foreign intelligence effort. The item frames this as raising key questions about implications for US-China relations, without further detail.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang at Centre of US-China Spy Row

items.summary: China's Global Times accused the New York Times of linking Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to spying without solid proof, warning it could strain China-US ties. Nvidia launched an independent probe; Trump defended Huang as a respected figure.
items.title: China Slams US Media Over Jensen Huang Spy Row

items.summary: A Hindi page lists five top stories, headlined by alleged Chinese spying tied to Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang after he admitted marital infidelity and drew U.S. congressional questions; it also covers record stubble-burning in Punjab during Diwali, an El Niño heat warning through 2027 per WMO, rising festival sweet prices reported by Bloomberg, and IRCTC's alert against ordering food online on trains.
items.title: Nvidia co-founder spy allegations lead Hindi news roundup

items.summary: Karam Kang and Mo Xiao analyze U.S. broadband deployment data from 2010 to 2019, finding that large internet service providers expand capacity more in electorally competitive counties. They associate greater provider capacity in swing counties with fewer subsequent entry- and investment-facilitating policies, particularly rights-of-way accommodations benefiting smaller providers.
items.title: Study Finds Broadband Firms May Shape Policy Through Investment

items.summary: Ana M. Gazmuri and Elena Prager study how peer exposure affects college applications using granular classroom-level data, finding that peers who apply raise application rates while admitted peers do not, consistent with an information mechanism; counterfactuals suggest the effect could close urban-rural and gender gaps.
items.title: Peer Influence in College Applications Study

items.summary: NPR reports that El Niño is expected to bring wild weather, but also business opportunity for some. Contractors are booked up as homeowners prepare for heavy rains and ski resorts gear up to cash in on snow.
items.title: El Niño Opens Weather-Driven Business Opportunities for Contractors and Resorts

items.summary: Jensen Huang's disclosed affair with an alleged Chinese spy has sent Nvidia's stock plunging and triggered internal and government investigations. Shares slid up to 8.8%, erasing nearly $400 billion in valuation after the Sunday memo disclosure. The board is assembling a committee of independent directors with outside counsel to investigate reports that Huang was targeted for foreign intelligence, as risks now threaten the whole AI industry.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Threatens Entire AI Industry, Not Just CEO

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over alleged ties to Chinese intelligence through a businesswoman with whom he had an intimate relationship. The company's board has launched an independent investigation. Nvidia says it has no reason to believe its trade secrets or US national security have been compromised, though shares fell around 5% in premarket trading on Monday following the news.
items.title: Nvidia launches independent probe into Jensen Huang's alleged Chinese intelligence links amid share drop

items.summary: Donald Trump said at a White House press conference that the war in Iran is 'effectively over,' playing down fears of renewed US military action after midterm elections. He cited positive momentum toward an end to the conflict and noted Israel and Gulf allies are protected from Iranian threats. The remarks followed Oval Office talks with Qatar's prime minister, who lobbied against resuming hostilities.
items.title: Trump Declares Iran War Effectively Over Amid Gulf Pressure

items.summary: France accuses Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps cyber unit, Shahid Kaveh, of launching destructive attacks on refrigeration controllers at around 700 retail sites and small hydroelectric plants in October. According to the French National Cybersecurity Agency, ANSSI, hackers raised temperatures overnight, spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food, while officials called it unprecedented in scale and aggression. The Paris Prosecutor's Office is seeking international arrest warrants. Iran has not responded. France says it identified the attackers through digital clues including Farsi-language traces. Experts say the strikes fit known Iranian tactics amid ongoing conflict with the United States.
items.title: France Accuses Iran of Sabotage in Refrigeration Cyberattacks

items.summary: Todd Russell, a survivor of the 2006 Beaconsfield goldmine collapse that entombed Larry Knight and Brant Webb for two weeks before their rescue, has died at age 54 after recently announcing deteriorating health. Tasmanian premier Jeremy Rockliff led tributes on Tuesday, praising Russell’s mental-health advocacy and his 31-year fire brigade career.
items.title: Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell dies aged 54

items.summary: Northern Ethiopia faces a strained healthcare system amid conflict, according to reporting on the situation there. The health care system was once regarded as a regional model. In the northern Tigray region, ongoing conflict has left health facilities and medical workers vulnerable to attacks.
items.title: Conflict strains healthcare system in northern Ethiopia's Tigray region

items.summary: Russian and Ukrainian envoys will discuss territorial issues and proposals for ceasefire monitoring during talks in the United Arab Emirates this week. A senior U.S. official briefed reporters anonymously Monday, noting daily discussions with both sides ahead of two days of scheduled negotiations beginning Tuesday in Abu Dhabi. The meeting resumes talks paused in February after a shift toward Iran.
items.title: Russian and Ukrainian envoys meet in UAE on ceasefire monitoring, territory

items.summary: M. John Harrison, 81, won the Booker Prize on Monday at a London ceremony for his novel The End of Everything, which explores an apocalypse shaped by artificial intelligence and post-Brexit Britain. Judge Mary Beard called it extraordinary in writing and ambition, while Harrison said current affairs inspired its satire.
items.title: Oldest Booker winner named for AI-themed novel

items.summary: Cross-examination continued in the NSW Supreme Court as Crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC pressed accused Beau Lamarre-Condon, who pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies. He described texts and screenshots of their December 2022 relationship while arguing he was never showing off his partner.
items.title: Live: Beau Lamarre-Condon faces grilling in cross-examination

items.summary: Victoria Police continue searching dense bushland near Walhalla East, Cowwarr in Gippsland for a 17-year-old teenager missing since Friday. He was camping with a friend when he walked away to collect supplies and became disoriented. Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said the teen is strong and fit and remains hopeful of finding him. About 80 emergency service personnel scoured the area yesterday, supported by helicopters, boats, motorbikes, horses and more than 50 people on foot. Authorities say they are throwing absolutely everything at the search and have no plans to scale it back soon.
items.title: Police Continue Search for Teenager Missing in Gippsland Bushland

items.summary: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the United States are set to meet Tuesday in Abu Dhabi for a new round of peace talks aimed at ending nearly five years of full-scale war triggered by Moscow's 2022 invasion. Security guarantees top the agenda, with US officials insisting that a broader European security architecture be part of any deal. Putin wants Ukraine to withdraw from annexed regions and abandon NATO membership; Zelensky rejects ceding territory and insists on direct talks between the two leaders. Fighting continues along the front line despite local truces.
items.title: Russia, Ukraine and US open trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi

items.summary: The judges praised M John Harrison’s satirical novel The End of Everything for its “extraordinary expert writing and huge ambition,” making him the oldest ever recipient. At a London ceremony, chair Mary Beard announced the winner alongside panelist Jarvis Cocker. Harrison said he had been working for 40 to 50 years to shift literary balance.
items.title: M John Harrison wins Booker Prize at age of sixty

items.summary: At COP17 in Yerevan, delegates began the first global review of progress toward the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework goals adopted in 2022. In a commentary authored by Madhu Rao and Nik Sekhran, the authors argue that rangers remain overlooked in policy despite being essential to effective conservation. Their research reviewed 45 documents including 21 national biodiversity strategies; references to area appeared roughly 70 times more often than references to rangers. They note annual global spending of around $24 billion is less than 40% of the roughly $68 billion needed each year, and that only 47% of rangers have insurance. The authors call for policies to formally recognize and fund rangers as a workforce critical to meeting targets like conserving 30% of land and waters by 2030.
items.title: Rangers Must Be Central to Biodiversity Conservation Commitments

items.summary: Representative Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, introduced a resolution Monday in the House of Representatives to launch impeachment proceedings against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The measure argues that Hegseth backed military operations lacking clear legal basis and strategic rationale. It must first pass a House vote, possibly as early as Wednesday, before moving to the Senate.
items.title: Republican lawmaker pushes impeachment vote on Hegseth

items.summary: President Duma Boko announced Monday that Botswana will double its stake in diamond producer De Beers to 30%, making the mineral-rich nation its single largest shareholder. Speaking to parliament in Gaborone, he said the move would give Botswana greater influence over decisions and expose it to technology through Element Six, De Beers' synthetic diamond business. Boko added that neighboring Namibia and Angola would also participate in the transaction backing a bid by the Global Diamond Consortium for an 85% stake put up for sale by Anglo American in 2024.
items.title: Botswana President Duma Boko Announces Doubling of De Beers Stake

items.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a sweeping overhaul of the Department of Defense's Professional Military Education system on Monday, directing reforms to prioritize combat readiness and warfighting skills. The directive follows a Senior Service College Task Force review and aims to reverse decades of 'academic drift' by eliminating ideological distractions in favor of joint warfighting mastery, strategic decision-making, and competitive military exercises.
items.title: Defense Secretary Orders Overhaul of Military Education

items.summary: Milo Quifes, 25, is one of the stars of La Bola Negra, directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi. The film has become the highest-grossing Spanish movie of the year and ranks among the 10 highest-grossing in the country’s history, with critics positioning it as a contender for Best Picture at the Oscars. Quifes describes his path from biology studies to TikTok fame to acting, shaped by anxiety that once kept him unable to leave home. He says he is tired of repeatedly coming out about his sexuality and credits the film’s queer cast for helping him find value in his experiences. The article draws on interviews with Quifes and casting directors Eva Leira and Yolanda Serrano, who describe his emotional intensity during auditions.
items.title: Actor Reflects on Breakout Role in Spanish Oscar Hope La Bola Negra

items.summary: An explosion at a steel plant in Izmir province killed 17 people on Monday, 9 November, according to the item. The blast occurred at 11:46am local time after an overhead crane collapsed into an electric arc furnace during maintenance work, damaging a gas line and triggering a fire. Around 200 employees were present when it happened. Five people have been detained as four prosecutors investigate.
items.title: Steel Plant Explosion Kills 17 in Turkey's Izmir Province

items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced on Sunday that Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, would be given a chance to form a new government. This follows nearly two weeks of political gridlock after what was described as Israel’s most consequential election failed to produce a clear winner. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to convene a stable coalition from the deeply divided opposition. Even if successful, his government faces major challenges including keeping the coalition together and escalating violence in the West Bank. He emphasized that “all of us will need to compromise”, though observers question whether cooperation with Arab parties is feasible given campaign promises not to join them.
items.title: Eisenkot Given Chance to Form Israeli Government Amid Coalition Uncertainty

items.summary: Poland's two leading political figures, Tusk and Nawrocki, attended a memorial for the six victims of the 7 November shooting in Kraków. They arrived together and placed candles among those already left by mourners before kneeling side by side while an officer played a horn. The ceremony came amid their bitter dispute over reforms to Poland's Constitutional Tribunal.
items.title: Polish Rivals Unite at Kraków Shooting Memorial

items.summary: Thick smog shrouded New Delhi on Monday, November 9, 2026, after firecrackers during Diwali compounded high pollution levels. The air quality index exceeded 350 in parts of the capital, reaching severe categories with health risks. Residents reported throat irritation and eye itching. Cooler weather, crop-residue fires from Punjab and Haryana, and stagnant conditions worsened haze over the city's more than 30 million people.
items.title: Smog Blankets New Delhi After Diwali Firecrackers Add to Pollution

items.summary: The Novaya Gazeta newspaper shut its Moscow office on Monday, saying it could not continue reporting amid a campaign of state pressure. Co-founded by Mikhail Gorbachev and long critical of the Kremlin's invasion of Ukraine, the outlet was branded a foreign agent and barred from processing reader donations. Founding editor Dmitry Muratov issued an appeal for free speech in wartime Russia.
items.title: Novaya Gazeta Closes Moscow Newsroom Amid State Pressure

items.summary: A decade after Prime Minister Narendra Modi withdrew all 500- and 1,000-rupee banknotes on November 8, 2016, the article examines whether demonetization delivered its promised cleanup of black money. The move invalidated 86.9% of currency in circulation but drew heavy hardship on queues, missed wages and deaths among vulnerable people. Experts Joe Athialy, Lekha Chakraborty and Arun Kumar say it penalized cash-dependent workers while leaving illicit wealth untouched, since much is held in property and gold. The Reserve Bank reported 99.3% of withdrawn notes returned by 2018. Digital payments grew sharply—UPI processed 241.6 billion transactions worth 314.2 trillion rupees—but banknotes still rose to 43.15 trillion rupees in October 2026, and Chakraborty warns that trend predated the ban.
items.title: Ten Years After India's Cash Ban, Promises Still Unmet

items.summary: US stocks rose Monday, with the S&P 500 up 2.34% and the Dow gaining about 1,104 points, as an easing in oil prices cooled inflation concerns. The Nasdaq added 2.73%. Shares had fallen sharply after Democrats won the midterms, raising fears of tighter AI regulation. Nvidia was the standout decliner amid questions over its leadership following a foreign-intelligence probe. Analysts at Morgan Stanley and UBS called last week’s selloff excessive. Investors now await inflation data on Tuesday and Friday.
items.title: US stocks rally as oil slide eases inflation fears; Nvidia falls

items.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday he spoke with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about reports that a Chinese businesswoman linked to him aided Beijing's espionage, asserting Huang had no idea she was a spy. The FBI is investigating the matter. Nvidia launched an independent probe into claims Huang faced foreign intelligence targeting; its shares fell to a seven-month low. China dismissed the allegations as unsubstantiated and a smear campaign.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Against Espionage Allegations

items.summary: A proposed class-action lawsuit accuses Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing alleged ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. The suit follows an independent board investigation into reports that Alice Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence via Megaspeed, which buys Nvidia's AI chips. China rejects the claims as baseless.
items.title: Nvidia and Jensen Huang Sued Over Alleged Chinese Spy Links, Shareholder Fraud Claims

items.summary: Forbes estimates Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's net worth at about $162.2 billion, which Sportschosun says his spouse could receive roughly half as marital property under California's community-property system—about $81.1 billion or over $62.6 billion in NVIDIA shares. The figures are labeled estimates and uncertain. Separately, US intelligence officials reportedly believe Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang of Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer under investigation for funneling chips to China; Huang told employees he was not faithful to his wife.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Divorce Settlement and Alleged China Ties

items.summary: Nvidia Corp. shares fell roughly 6 per cent in premarket trading after its board launched an investigation into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, following his admission of an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence agencies of spying for China. The stock was down about 22 per cent from its October high as the inquiry raised leadership uncertainty ahead of quarterly earnings on Nov. 17.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Drop After Board Launches Probe Into CEO Jensen Huang

items.summary: A Google policy head told a Senate hearing that Australia's proposed Digital Duty of Care law could force the company to block under-18s from Gmail. The bill, which has passed the House but still needs cross-party support in the Senate, would fine companies up to A$109 million ($75.1 million) for failing to remove harmful content. Google and other platforms argue it gives regulators too much discretion and risks over-moderation.
items.title: Google Warns Australian Internet Safety Bill Could Block Under-18s From Gmail

items.summary: Stand-up comedian Gaurav Gupta faced heavy online criticism after his appearance on the reality show Bigg Boss 20, in which he targeted contestants Scout OP and Love Gill with personal jokes. The remarks drew displeasure from both contestants and fans, who felt they crossed into unfair attacks on their private lives. Amid the backlash, Gupta made his Instagram account private without issuing a formal statement.
items.title: Comedian Gaurav Gupta Locks Instagram After Bigg Boss 20 Backlash

items.summary: An investigation by the Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo found that more than 150 Chinese nationals have been livestreaming from a low-income neighbourhood in Uttara, north of Dhaka, while presenting it to their audiences as life in India. The streamers broadcast on platforms such as WeChat and Douyin, using local guides paid Tk 700 to Tk 800 daily. Residents report that the broadcasts have sparked anger over privacy violations, though police say language barriers hinder any action.
items.title: Chinese Livestreamers in Dhaka Deceive Viewers About Delhi

items.summary: The Congress-led Kerala government began collecting petrol samples Monday to test whether their ethanol content exceeds the prescribed 20%, mirroring Karnataka's move and raising a possible Centre-state clash over E20 fuel. State food and civil supplies minister Rizwan Arshad dismissed objections from three oil marketing companies as 'illogical', accusing them of seeking another joint survey after recalibrating the mix.
items.title: Kerala government begins ethanol content checks on petrol

items.summary: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies recommended a definitive anti-dumping duty of up to USD 565 per one lakh pieces, ranging from USD 442 to USD 565 per one lakh pieces, on medical examination rubber gloves imported from Thailand and Malaysia for five years. The probe followed applications by Navco Industries and Wadi Surgicals and found the nascent domestic industry suffered material injury. The finance ministry will decide; DGTR said the duty would not significantly affect users or consumers and would restore fair competition.
items.title: India's DGTR Recommends Anti-Dumping Duty on Rubber Gloves From Thailand and Malaysia

items.summary: The US-created Board of Peace warned Monday of an immediate humanitarian emergency in the Gaza Strip after severe seasonal flooding swamped tens of thousands of tents. It blamed both Israel for insufficient supply authorization and Hamas for failing to honor peace commitments, while calling on Israeli forces—who control around 65% of the territory—to withdraw as part of a stalled rebuilding plan.
items.title: Board of Peace Blames Israel and Hamas Over Gaza Flood Emergency

items.summary:
Citi cut its rating on US stocks, including the Nasdaq, to neutral as an AI sell-off erased about $3 trillion from S&P 500 companies. Strategists led by Beata Manthey warned index positioning could fall into net-short territory. The downgrade follows Democrat midterm wins and rising fears that stricter data-centre regulations may slow AI infrastructure buildout. Citi also cut global and European technology ratings to neutral, while raising healthcare and food stocks.

visual null
items.title: Citi Downgrades US Stocks Amid AI Sell-off and Regulatory Fears

items.summary: The Kerala government announced November 16 as the launch date for Toofan Care, the next phase of its anti-narcotics campaign Operation Toofan. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the initiative will shift emphasis toward rehabilitating people with drug addiction through treatment and counselling at 35 hospitals prepared across the state. The government says enforcement alone cannot solve the problem. Data cited by ANI shows Kerala recorded 30,697 NDPS Act cases in 2023, the highest among Indian states; police registered 10,070 cases and arrested 10,883 people under the campaign by September. Chennithala claimed the first phase reduced drug use by 20-30%. He also said alleged loopholes in the NDPS Act had been raised with Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
items.title: Kerala Launches Rehabilitation Phase of Anti-Drug Campaign on November 16

items.summary: The High Court at Gwalior refused to quash an FIR arising from a Sept 15, 2023 shootout near Sirol district, where suspects fired shots and one bullet struck a labourer below the navel. Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta dismissed the petition under Section 528 BNSS (Section 482 CrPC), holding that allegations of firing with intent to kill disclose a serious offence affecting society at large; thus a compromise alone cannot invoke inherent jurisdiction or quash the case.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court Rejects FIR Quash on Compromise in Firearm Case
